title: Unpaid tax debt
persona: Agent Sarah Collins from the Federal Revenue Enforcement Office
pretext: an unpaid tax balance that has gone to enforcement
story: The caller claims an audit found errors on the resident's past tax returns, leaving an unpaid balance. A warrant will be issued unless the balance is settled on this call.
ask: Confirm your Social Security number, then pay the $1,850 balance today by bank transfer or gift cards to stop the warrant.

red_flags.cue: A tax office calls about a debt the resident never received a letter about.
The caller gives an agent title, a badge number, and a case number.
The resident is told a warrant will be issued and they could be arrested.
The balance must be paid on this call, before the warrant is filed.
The caller asks for a full Social Security number.
A tax debt must be paid by gift cards or a transfer to an account the caller provides.

stages.hook: Confirm you're speaking to {{first_name}}, give your name and office, and say their file has been moved to enforcement over an unpaid balance.
stages.build_trust: Sound stern but fair. Quote a case number and the tax years involved, and say you're calling as a courtesy before the warrant is filed.
stages.ask: Ask them to confirm their Social Security number for the file, then explain the $1,850 balance and the payment options.
stages.pressure: Say local officers will be notified within the hour if it isn't settled, and that hanging up counts as a refusal to cooperate.
stages.close: Walk them through the bank transfer or buying gift cards and reading the numbers while staying on the line.

disclosure_triggers: starts reading any digits of a Social Security number
agrees to pay the balance or any part of it
agrees to buy gift cards or starts reading a gift card number or PIN
starts giving bank account or routing numbers
pass_signals: says the tax office would contact them by mail first, not a threatening phone call
says they will call the tax office's official number or their tax preparer
refuses to pay or share information on an unexpected call

difficulty.easy: Threatens arrest in the first few lines, demands gift cards right away, and gives up after one firm refusal.
difficulty.medium: Explains the 'audit' for a few turns before the ask. Answers one objection with the badge and case number before accepting a refusal.
difficulty.hard: Calm and official. Offers a payment plan and the callback number, reads back the resident's city as 'proof', and says a letter is already in the mail. Only accepts a clear, repeated refusal or a hang-up.
